title: feat(spec): ListColumn gains `prefix` and the `{ type, field }` summary form (objectui#2231)
body:
## Summary

Two `ListColumn` capabilities the ObjectUI grid renderer has shipped for a while were absent from the protocol, so they survived as a local `.extend()` fork in `@object-ui/types` — the drift [objectui#2231](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/2231) is closing. objectui [#2882](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/2882) (phase 2) reduced that package's hand-written mirrors to spec re-exports and left exactly these two fields as **sanctioned local extensions, flagged for promotion**. This is that promotion — the protocol side of a `declared ≠ enforced` gap read backwards: the renderer enforced more than the spec declared.

## What changed — `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`

- **`ColumnPrefixSchema`** (new) → `ListColumn.prefix`. Airtable-style compound cells: render a second field's value inline before the cell value (a status badge in front of the record name), so a list carries two signals in one column instead of spending a second column on it. `{ field, type?: 'badge' | 'text' }`, `type` defaulting to `'text'`.
- **`ColumnSummaryConfigSchema`** (new) → broadens `ListColumn.summary` to `ColumnSummarySchema | { type, field? }`. The object form is for a footer that aggregates a field **other** than the column's own (an `amount` column summing `amount_in_base_currency`). The shorthand `summary: 'sum'` is unchanged and remains the common case.
  - `type` reuses `ColumnSummarySchema` rather than restating a narrower enum, so both forms share **one** aggregation vocabulary and cannot drift apart. (The objectui-side fork had narrowed it to 5 of the 11 functions — precisely the kind of second dialect Prime Directive #12 warns about.)
- New type exports: `ColumnPrefix`, `ColumnSummaryConfig`.
- `json-schema.manifest.json` regenerated (`pnpm gen:schema`) — adds `ui/ColumnPrefix` and `ui/ColumnSummaryConfig`.

## Both are already honored by the renderer

- `prefix` — `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` wraps the cell renderer when `prefix.field` is set, rendering `badge` through the `select` cell renderer and anything else as muted text.
- `summary.field` — `packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts` resolves `const targetField = config.field || col.field` and aggregates that field.

No new renderer behavior ships here; this only lets the protocol describe what the renderer already does.

## Compatibility

Additive. Every previously valid `ListColumn` still parses — `summary` gains a union arm, `prefix` is optional. No consumer reads either field off the spec type today (objectui reached them through its local extension), so nothing downstream needs to change before the next release.

## Verification

- `packages/spec`: full suite **258 files / 6717 tests** green, including 7 new cases in `view.test.ts` covering both summary forms across the whole `ColumnSummarySchema` vocabulary, the `prefix` default, and the rejection paths (`summary: 'median'`, `{ type: 'median' }`, `prefix: {}`, `prefix.type: 'chip'`).
- `pnpm gen:schema` re-run; the manifest diff is exactly the two new definitions.

## Follow-up (objectui side, blocked on this release)

Once `@objectstack/spec` publishes, `@object-ui/types` drops its `ListColumnSchema.extend({ prefix, summary })` and the schema becomes a plain re-export; its parity guard's `SANCTIONED_LOCAL` set for `ListColumn` goes empty. Tracked under objectui#2231.

Separately surfaced while auditing this: `useColumnSummary`'s `computeAggregation` implements only `count`/`sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max`, so the other six spec aggregations (`count_empty`, `count_filled`, `count_unique`, `percent_empty`, `percent_filled`, `none`) currently compute `null` in the grid — a renderer-side `declared ≠ enforced` gap, filed on the objectui side rather than fixed here.
